importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is significant — single-room units, multi-room blocks, double-storey structures, and configurations with attached toilets are visually distinct. Buyers use the image to confirm they are looking at an RCC concrete structure rather than a steel cabin or PUF panel prefab; wrong structure type is an immediate skip.

Room configuration, number of floors, toilet facility, and wall material are non-interchangeable requirements — a dormitory layout cannot substitute for individual rooms, and a single-storey unit cannot substitute for a G+2 block. Specs drive the shortlist before any price comparison occurs.

Per-sq-ft rate is the primary comparison metric for Indian contractors who compare aggressively across sellers once spec fit is confirmed. Price varies substantially with configuration — single-room vs double-storey, with or without toilet, flooring type — making it a hard shortlisting gate after spec confirmation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per piece (single precast room unit) or lump sum (full labour colony project); per sq ft is dominant but the mix creates genuine price comparison confusion if unit is not shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared without knowing the unit — a per-sq-ft listing and a per-piece listing for the same room size are not directly comparable. Unit ambiguity is a real market problem in this category.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No recognised brand names exist with buyer recall in this category; market is fragmented across regional precast manufacturers in Agra, Faridabad, and Surat belts — buyers search by spec and price, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Seller track record, installation capability, and geographic reach matter because the product includes transportation and on-site assembly — an unknown seller with no installation history is a risk. However, specs and price carry greater weight than company identity in the initial shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Single-floor vs G+1/G+2/G+3 are non-interchangeable structural configurations with very large price deltas — multi-storey structures require different foundations, structural loads, and construction costs that cannot be substituted.

Single, double, and dormitory layouts are non-interchangeable room configurations that determine internal partition design, door/window count, and per-sq-ft cost — a dormitory hall cannot substitute for individual rooms on a site requiring privacy.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Standard room dimensions (11ft×11ft, 11ft×15ft, 11ft×22ft) are the primary sizing input for per-sq-ft quotations — buyers specify required room dimensions and sellers cannot generate an accurate price without this information.

RCC panel thickness (3-inch vs 4-inch) determines structural strength, thermal performance, and per-sq-ft material cost — a meaningful differentiator between economy and standard-grade RCC labour quarters.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Directly defines the layout and amenity level of the unit — a seller needs this to determine internal partition design, plumbing requirements, and per-sq-ft cost; a dormitory and a room with attached toilet are fundamentally different products requiring different manufacturing inputs.
Determines structural complexity, foundation requirements, and total project cost — a seller cannot quote accurately without knowing whether the buyer needs a single-storey or multi-storey structure.

missing_important_specs.why_important: The per-sq-ft quotation model requires sellers to know the required room dimensions or total built-up area — without this, a seller cannot generate any price at all, making it the most critical missing input in the RFQ form.
